This is now the annoying work-around I found after way too many tries... With that I think all of the `cupy_tests` (not slow) actually pass wth `pytest-run-parallel` (with or without free-threaded).
(EDIT: `cupy_tests/core_tests`, I guess I hadn't run the fully `cupy_tests`)

Of course, nothing is ever 100%, the more threads the hihgher the chance to find issues (and right now we know there are dead-locks in the allocator that I might have seen over many runs).

Running in CI I have to still think about, running most tests in many threads is likely too slow for us here.

requested_changes.body:
This will probably fixed in Python, but doesn't hurt even now. It is the one true bug-fix here (except on future 3.14.x versions presumably).

It seems my very long odyssey was caused by `defaultdict`. The mechanism is that two threads can inintialize a defaultdict at the same time.
In that case, one thread will get a `SingleDeviceMemoryPool` that is immediately discarded again. Howver, `SingleDEviceMemoryPool` owns the actual allocations currently which causes havoc later.
(And at least often not all that obvious havoc...)
